# A mark names a declaration the program still declares itself, so a backend
# that emits that declaration keeps spelling it its own way. Go emits the
# struct type, so honouring the mark's name here would leave two names for one
# type — `api.Item` used, `Entry` declared — and no import of the package the
# mark named, which nothing resolved.

sngl generate --lang=go --platform=bubbletea --out=out app.sngl
exists out/model.go

# One name, declared and used.
grep 'type Entry struct' out/model.go
grep 'Entry\{Title: "hello"\}' out/model.go
! grep 'api\.Item' out/model.go

# And nothing imported the package the mark named.
! grep 'example.com/api' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

#[foreign("go:example.com/api", "api.Item")]
struct Entry {
    title string
}

component main {
    var e = Entry{title = "hello"}
    text(value=e.title)
}
